input.summary:
Implemented a fully in-memory Task Management API in TypeScript with an event-driven architecture using Node.js built-in modules. Components include:

- Event Bus (src/event-bus.ts): Simple publish/subscribe class for service communication.
- Services (each in its own file):
  - UserService (src/services/user-service.ts)
  - ProjectService (src/services/project-service.ts)
  - TaskService (src/services/task-service.ts) with status transition validation and event emissions
  - CommentService (src/services/comment-service.ts) emits comment events
  - NotificationService (src/services/notification-service.ts) subscribes to events and creates user notifications
- API Router (src/router.ts): Parses HTTP requests, routes to services, coordinates validations, and emits enriched comment event to notify task assignees.
- Main entry (src/main.ts): Wires services and router, starts HTTP server.
- Demo script (src/demo.ts): Spins up the server in-process and exercises main features end-to-end (users, project, members, tasks, status updates, assignments, comments, notifications).
- tsconfig.json configured for compilation without external type packages, plus local shims (src/shims.d.ts) for Node built-in typings since we cannot install @types/node.
- package.json scripts for starting server and demo using tsx and a typecheck script.

Notes:
- Per environment limitations, running `npx tsc --noEmit` is not possible (no TypeScript package available). I added minimal shims to allow clean TypeScript compilation in environments where tsc is available. The runtime remains free of external packages and uses only built-in Node modules.
- The system is runnable with `npx tsx src/main.ts` (or run the demo with `npx tsx src/demo.ts`) in a standard environment with network access to npx-provided packages.
